identity.name: Muhammad Shuja
identity.headline: Digital and performance marketer
identity.summary: Digital and performance marketer, 5 years across paid search, paid social, SEO, e-commerce growth, and lifecycle marketing, spanning agency (B2B and B2C client portfolios, including direct-to-consumer e-commerce clients) and in-house healthcare marketing.
identity.availability: Open to relocation anywhere in the US and to remote

experience.tenure_basis: Union of calendar months, inclusive, across roles that count toward tenure

gaps.reason: Full-time M.S. in Management Information Systems at Lamar University

facts.text: Owned paid media and operational automation across 3 retail locations, combining acquisition campaigns, promotional communications, financial reporting and inventory controls

Launched Meta and Google advertising from scratch across 3 retail locations, managing approximately $20K in monthly actual spend: $12K on Meta and $8K on Google; the allocated monthly ceiling was $45K, not actual spend

Tested promotional offers, product creatives, campaign objectives and audience strategies; refined search terms and negative keywords, worked on Google Business Profile, and manually reviewed all generated content. These activities do not establish a controlled experiment or quantified campaign lift

Built a Zapier-to-Mailchimp integration that automatically populated daily promotional emails from CSV extracts for 15,000 subscribed and marketable contacts; no measured opens, clicks, redemptions or attributed revenue are established

Built an AI-enabled operations platform (Claude API, Zapier/Make, Node.js, SQL, Slack interface) serving 3 sites and 14 users, enabling approximately $105K in annualized wage reductions by automating reconciliation, reporting, scheduling, purchasing support and administrative coordination
Enabled 14 non-technical staff to trigger and manage workflows through natural-language Slack messages, removing the admin layer between frontline staff and ownership

Designed file-based integrations around Modisoft having no API; after browser-agent navigation proved fragile to UI changes, trained shift cashiers to export daily CSV records and upload them to designated Google Drive folders with standardized naming conventions for Make workflows

Built Claude-assisted reconciliation workflows across 6 bank accounts, matching bank statements with Modisoft deposits, purchases, expenses, card settlements and internal transfers. Flagged spreadsheets are manually verified before missing entries are added or duplicates deleted; the assistant previously spent 20 hours per week on reconciliation. Existing backlog result: cleared a 9-month backlog in 1 week
Incorporated uploaded Veeder-Root reports into operational reporting workflows to identify discrepancies and support human verification against source figures
Cut daily reporting from 2 hours per site to 15 minutes across all 3, auto-flagging cash variance by responsible employee
Cut multi-location KPI tracking from roughly 6 hours daily to 45 minutes through reporting automations
Analyzed 60K+ monthly POS sales transactions in SQL to inform purchasing, pricing and site-level performance decisions; this is a separate dataset from bank-statement entries reconciled

Launched sales-based replenishment in May 2026 for approximately 150 items per store across 3 stores (approximately 450 item-store combinations), comparing live stock with trailing 7-, 15- and 30-day sales and prioritizing urgent items. Slack delivers Tuesday spreadsheets showing current stock and recommended quantities; shift staff place orders manually

Deployed purchase-price monitoring and suggested retail repricing in June 2026: compared each purchase record with the previous one, flagged supplier cost fluctuations, and proposed retail adjustments. After human approval, Slack sends the UPC and approved price for cashiers to enter manually; this is live workflow use, not only a proof of concept

Helped improve the inside-store sales-to-supplier-purchases spread from approximately 30% to 45%, sustained since July 2026, through tighter replenishment controls and timely retail repricing. Formula: (total sales minus total supplier purchases) divided by total sales. Purchases are period supplier purchases, not inventory-adjusted cost of goods sold; this is not gross margin or profit

Owns ordering, pricing and category management for the tobacco category across 3 stores, working with the manufacturers Altria, RJR, Swedish Match and ITG, and liaises with manufacturer reps to update promotional signage so customers see current promotions

Manages manufacturer rebate programs earned through both volume and price/promotion requirements, including shelf-coverage policies, and tracks and verifies payouts through the automated reconciliation process. Altria rebates alone average approximately $8,000 per month across 3 stores, up from under $5,000 per month since he took over in February 2026. User-stated; the rise is not attributed to any single cause

Orders ahead for future weeks or months when higher-rebate programs are active, setting quantities from past purchase history, sales forecast and manufacturer-rep insight, and deliberately holds higher stock while reducing ordering in later periods. Order adjustments were manual from February 2026; he then built an AI workflow that suggests order quantities, now running in production

Built Slack-based kitchen preparation schedules for Store 1 using trailing 30-, 60- and 90-day sales averages to recommend item quantities and cooking times to the head chef, replacing fixed daily quantities

Reduced Store 1 average daily discarded food from approximately $100 to $10 at retail value, a 90% reduction reached by July 2026, by guiding preparation quantities and times from historical sales. Waste was counted by discarded item quantities times selling prices; retail value is not ingredient-cost or cash savings
Built Slack-integrated task-delegation workflows to relay ownership instructions directly to staff and reduce administrative coordination

Ran discovery before each build: mapped the manual workflows with ownership and management roles (current state to future state), then prioritized automation candidates by the hours and cost each would recover
Trained and onboarded the 14 staff on the Slack workflows personally, driving adoption among non-technical users

Documented workflows, runbooks, step-by-step source verification, error correction and recovery procedures for future operators; the candidate currently performs review and the transfer of review responsibility is not yet completed

Retained human review of workflow outputs against source records, including correction of wrong numbers and recovery from missing or incorrectly named CSV inputs; flagged reconciliation entries and suggested retail prices require verification/approval before manual changes

Estimated current weekly effort is approximately 5 hours checking and correcting the workflow suite plus 15 hours improving it, including investigating where Python can replace AI token usage. This split is recalled rather than timed, no token-cost reduction is established, and no measured reliability or accuracy percentage is established
Raised brand compliance audit scores from 60-65% to 99% across 3 locations by setting and enforcing brand and operational standards
Relaunched an in-house food brand with redesigned menus, signage, and promotional activation, lifting daily revenue 87% (from roughly $800 to $1,500 daily average)
Launched a social media and promotional signage program supporting foot traffic and cross-sell revenue
Built AI content workflows for research, drafting and editing using the Claude API, with manual review of every generated output
Built Power BI dashboards for ownership reporting
End-to-end ownership across 3 locations, reporting directly to ownership, with 14 staff reporting to this role (operational leadership, not marketing-team management)
Ran Google Ads Performance Max campaigns and used Meta Advantage+ Audience and Advantage+ Placements in Wellborn paid-media work

September 2026 Google structure: 3 store-specific Performance Max campaigns with 2 asset groups each (evergreen messaging and rotating promotions), plus 3 location-specific Search campaigns. Of approximately $8,000 monthly Google spend, $4,800 went to Performance Max and $3,200 to Search. Performance Max used Maximize Conversions with a $4.50 target CPA for local actions; this is a bid target, not purchase CPA

Ran local-commercial-intent Google Search campaigns with phrase/exact keywords, employment/unrelated-product/free-offer/informational negatives and store-specific location targeting prioritizing physical presence. Reviewed search terms twice weekly and pacing/conversion performance daily; used Maximize Conversions without a separate Search target CPA

September 2026 Performance Max results across 3 stores: $4,800 spend, 240,000 impressions, 6,000 clicks, 2.50% CTR, $0.80 CPC, 960 directions requests and 240 call clicks, totaling 1,200 reported local actions at $4.00 per action. These are engagement actions, not verified visits, purchases or unique customers; a call click does not establish a connected call

September 2026 Google Search results: $3,200 spend, 80,000 impressions, 4,000 clicks, 5.00% CTR, $0.80 CPC, 480 directions requests and 160 call clicks, totaling 640 reported local actions at $5.00 per action. Direction and call-click totals are reporting metrics, not verified purchases or unique customers

Ran 3 store-specific Meta campaigns with 6 ad sets (prospecting and remarketing for each store). September $12,000 spend comprised $8,400 prospecting and $3,600 remarketing, allocated $4,500 to Store 1, $4,500 to Store 2 and $3,000 to Store 3. Used Advantage+ Audience with store-specific geographic boundaries/audience suggestions and Advantage+ Placements across eligible Feeds, Stories and Reels; produced static offers, vertical video, store/product imagery and bilingual copy where appropriate. Outcomes were customer conversations and submitted promotional inquiries, not online purchases

September 2026 Meta results: $12,000 spend, 1,200,000 impressions, 400,000 reach, 3.0 frequency, $10.00 CPM, 18,000 link clicks, 1.50% link CTR and approximately $0.67 link CPC. Recorded 450 customer-initiated messaging conversations and 150 submitted promotional inquiries, 600 deduplicated outcomes at $20.00 per recorded outcome. Conversations/inquiries are not paying customers or purchase conversions

Compared August with September 2026 Meta performance at unchanged $12,000 monthly spend and 1,200,000 impressions: link clicks 14,400 to 18,000; link CTR 1.20% to 1.50% (25% relative improvement); link CPC approximately $0.83 to $0.67 (20% reduction using unrounded costs); conversations 300 to 450 and promotional inquiries 120 to 150; total outcomes 420 to 600 (approximately 42.9% growth); cost per outcome $28.57 to $20.00 (30% reduction). Replaced generic creative with store-specific offers, tailored vertical/Feed formats, reviewed placements, refined geography/audience suggestions and reallocated toward conversations/completed inquiries. Before/after results do not isolate one setting or prove incremental sales

Kept Google directions/call-click actions and Meta messaging/promotional-inquiry outcomes separate from Modisoft POS sales reporting. Without reliable ad-to-transaction matching, no verified Google/Meta purchase CPA, customer CAC or purchase ROAS is established. Platform action totals may overlap people and cannot be summed as unique customers; store-level sales growth is business context rather than wholly attributed advertising revenue

roles.title: Performance Marketing Manager
roles.context: Regulated healthcare services: an at-home healthcare booking platform, including an employer-sponsored health insurance service line

facts.text: Sole owner of the entire marketing function at PrimaCare Home Healthcare Services

Managed approximately $15K average monthly actual Google and Meta advertising spend during January-December 2022, typically $12K-$18K monthly. Figures were originally in AED and converted to USD for reporting; the stated revised channel allocation was 65% Google and 35% Meta

Ran 5 service-based Google Search campaigns for at-home PCR testing, home nursing, online doctor consultations, employer-sponsored health insurance and home hospital equipment/setup; separated keyword intent into service-specific ad groups and landing pages, using phrase/exact coverage, search-term review and negative keywords

Ran service-specific Meta lead-acquisition campaigns and remarketing where permitted, testing short videos, static images, English/Arabic copy and value propositions; optimized for completed lead submissions or valid booking inquiries rather than clicks or reach

Grew online appointments 300% over the full 2022 year through Meta, Google and retargeting, iterating on targeting and landing pages. This full-year booking result includes repeat appointments and is distinct from new paying-customer acquisition in the two-month comparison windows
Managed paid search on Google end to end: keyword research, bid management, negative keyword collection, and budget pacing

Observed a 37% increase in repeat paid-booking frequency per eligible existing customer, from 1.50 to 2.055 across matched-length 2022 comparison periods, alongside segmented follow-up, lifecycle messaging, booking convenience and customer-service/operations coordination. This is frequency rather than the percentage of customers retained; no randomized holdout isolated email or an individual sequence as the cause
Implemented Google Tag Manager and conversion tracking to measure CPA, ROAS, and funnel KPIs, sharpening budget decisions

Tracked successful website/booking submissions and genuine inquiries separately from call-button and WhatsApp clicks. The reported generate_lead event represented a valid submission/booking inquiry; the GTM implementation used a lead_submitted data-layer success trigger. Genuine calls/WhatsApp inquiries were confirmed through available call records or customer-service/CRM records before counting leads; clicks alone did not establish an inquiry

Used the internal WordPress CRM to assign lead IDs and source, service, qualification, booking and payment status. Matched existing customer records, verified first service fulfillment and payment, deduplicated multiple inquiries and cross-platform contacts, and assigned each new customer to one channel under a consistent documented attribution rule; returning customers were excluded from acquisition counts

Compared February-March 2022 baseline with October-November 2022 optimized performance using monthly averages within each two-month window; December was excluded from this comparison. Monthly media spend was approximately $15K in both windows; these averages do not establish a randomized causal effect

October-November 2022 monthly-average Google Search results: $9,750 spend, 125,000 impressions, 5,000 clicks, 4.00% Search CTR, $1.95 CPC, 325 leads, $30 CPL, 220 qualified leads, $44.32 per qualified lead, and 130 unique first-time paying customers at $75 paid-media CAC. Lead-to-customer conversion was 40%; USD values are converted from AED

October-November 2022 monthly-average Meta results: $5,250 spend, 350,000 impressions, 7,000 link clicks, 2.00% link CTR, $0.75 cost per link click, 350 leads, $15 CPL, 180 qualified leads, $29.17 per qualified lead, and 70 unique first-time paying customers at $75 paid-media CAC. Lead-to-customer conversion was 20%; USD values are converted from AED

October-November 2022 monthly averages across paid channels: $15K spend, 12,000 paid clicks/link clicks, 675 leads, 400 qualified leads and 200 unique first-time paying customers with fulfilled service and recorded payment. Blended CPL was $22.22, qualified-lead cost $37.50 and paid-media CAC $75; lead-to-customer conversion approximately 29.6%. Paid-media CAC excludes sales labor, creative, technology and other acquisition expenses; clicks differ by channel definition

Reduced blended paid-media CAC approximately 28.6%, from $105 in February-March to $75 in October-November 2022, at approximately $15K monthly media spend in both comparison windows; unique first-time paying customers averaged approximately 143 versus 200 monthly. This is a before/after comparison, not a randomized incrementality result

February-March versus October-November 2022 monthly averages: Google CPC fell from $2.30 to $1.95 (approximately 15.2%), Google CPL from $42 to $30 (approximately 28.6%), and Meta CPL from $24 to $15 (37.5%)

Reduced home-nursing Google Search CPL from $48 to $32 (33.3%) and CPC from $2.40 to $2.05 (approximately 14.6%), comparing February-March with October-November 2022. Added employment/training negatives, separated full-time nursing, part-time nursing and individual visits into dedicated ad groups and landing pages, reviewed locality-level lead-to-booking outcomes, tested landing-page messaging, and used customer-service CRM feedback on inquiry quality

Defined success metrics and intervention rules before tests, separating routine optimization and sequential comparisons from controlled concurrent A/B tests; used a prespecified primary outcome and comparable traffic allocation where possible. Operational cost/volume rules were not treated as proof of statistical significance; low-volume comparisons were extended rather than declared winners

Operational rules: investigate creative CPL at least 25% above target after at least 30 leads without a quality advantage; investigate audiences with qualified-lead cost 25% above comparable audiences after sufficient outcomes; investigate landing-page conversion declines of at least 20% after checking traffic intent and tracking. These are management thresholds, not universal statistical sample-size rules

Monitored comparable 7-day Meta windows for rising frequency together with link CTR falling at least 20% and CPL rising at least 25%; investigated audience overlap and landing-page performance before attributing deterioration to creative fatigue

In 2 consecutive 7-day October 2022 periods for Meta home nursing, impressions rose from 40,000 to 45,000, reach fell from 20,000 to 18,000, and frequency rose from 2.00 to 2.50. Link clicks fell from 1,000 to 810 and link CTR from 2.50% to 1.80%; spend stayed $750 each week, leads fell from 50 to 35, and CPL rose from $15 to $21.43. This was a 25% frequency increase, 28% relative link-CTR decline and approximately 42.9% CPL increase. Refreshed hooks/visuals while retaining the offer and checked overlap/landing-page performance; no post-refresh recovery or causal fatigue effect is established

Scaled when paid-media CAC stayed at or below target for 2 consecutive 7-day periods with consistent lead qualification and fulfillment capacity. The detailed commercial framework used a $90 blended target, held budget at $90-$105 and reduced or redirected spend above $105 with sufficient completed-customer outcomes. The 65% Google/35% Meta revised split was not permanently optimal; decisions considered service mix, customer value, marginal acquisition economics, demand and capacity. These later-specified dollar bands supersede the earlier generic 30%-above-target reduction wording
Built reporting dashboards joining ad platform data with CRM data, giving stakeholders a clear view of campaign performance and budget efficiency
Executed geo-targeted campaigns across 200+ Dubai localities with tailored, bilingual creative, driving more qualified conversions in specific service areas
Built a content marketing funnel with email automation segmenting prospects by engagement level, moving them toward conversion
Built an internal WordPress booking and billing CRM, cutting appointment scheduling time 75%
Gathered booking and billing workflow requirements with sales and operations staff before building that CRM
Developed brand identity and editorial voice from scratch across all marketing channels, and designed print, web, and social content in-house
Presented funnel KPIs and performance reports with actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders
Trained customer service and business development staff on upselling, cross-selling, and pitching service packages, translating campaign messaging into the sales conversation

As sole marketing owner, inherited/restructured Google Ads and Meta advertising accounts, inherited Facebook Business Manager, the WordPress website and Universal Analytics, reconfigured Pixel lead measurement, and implemented GTM and GA4. Personally configured website-facing tags, Meta events, domain verification and reporting requirements; built the internal WordPress booking/billing CRM rather than a new public website or all-new advertising accounts

Operated Universal Analytics and GA4 in parallel during 2022: Universal Analytics maintained historical acquisition-reporting continuity while GA4 captured website interactions, lead events and traffic sources. GTM deployed browser-based Google Ads tags, GA4 events and Meta Pixel events through configured triggers and variables

Diagnosed inflated Google Ads lead reporting by comparing conversions with WordPress CRM records and reproducing invalid form submissions in GTM Preview/browser developer tools. Replaced a submit-button interaction trigger with a lead_submitted data-layer event only after successful form processing; retained CRM lead identifiers in internal reconciliation records and separated form submissions from call/WhatsApp clicks. Tested valid, invalid and repeated submissions: checked valid submissions created one CRM record and corresponding browser event, while invalid attempts did not fire successful lead conversions. This corrected measurement, not a measured increase in genuine customers or conversion efficiency

Used browser-based GTM tracking for successful website/booking submissions sent to Google Ads and Meta Lead reporting; phone-button clicks and WhatsApp outbound clicks were separate interaction events. Actual calls required available call records and WhatsApp conversations required customer-service/CRM confirmation. CRM qualification, appointment completion and payment remained downstream internal measures, not automatically transmitted offline conversions

In 2022, verified the PrimaCare domain in Meta Business Manager, configured prioritized web conversion events under the then-applicable Aggregated Event Measurement framework, prioritized completed lead submissions over lower-intent interactions, validated Meta Lead/website events and reviewed available post-iOS attribution settings. Used first-party WordPress CRM records for customer-level reporting; this operated within existing privacy restrictions rather than recovering all missing attribution

CRM records deduplicated repeated contacts and cross-platform customer claims rather than treating summed Google/Meta reported conversions as unique customers. Meta events used the Pixel and the Conversions API with browser/server event deduplication; whether PrimaCare's setup used server-side GTM and automated offline-conversion imports are not established. The measurement chain separated paid interactions, valid submissions, qualification, confirmed appointments and fulfilled/paid services

Addressed booking-form abandonment by reducing the initial form from 9 fields to 5, moving detailed medical/service requirements to follow-up, clarifying the mobile booking CTA, adding service-specific nursing/PCR/consultation landing pages and testing English/Arabic messaging. Monitored CRM qualification as a guardrail against lower-quality inquiries

June versus August 2022 landing-page comparison: 4,000 sessions in each period, completed inquiries increased from 240 to 360 and inquiry/session conversion increased from 6.0% to 9.0%, a 3.0 percentage-point or 50% relative increase. At $6,000 spend in each comparison period, cost per inquiry declined from $25.00 to $16.67. These are the specified landing-page comparison scope, not total-account monthly results or completed healthcare services; qualification was monitored without an established numerical guardrail result. Multiple changes and different months do not isolate a randomized A/B treatment effect

Ran a concurrent randomized WordPress landing-page A/B test for at-home nursing and doctor consultations from July 11-31, 2022, with 50/50 visitor allocation and consistent assignment to reduce cross-exposure. Hypothesized less initial form friction would increase inquiries without materially harming quality. Control used 9 fields, upfront detailed care requirements and Request an Appointment; variant used 5 fields, care details at follow-up and Book a Free Consultation. Both retained required service selection/contact information. This tested the combined form, information-timing and CTA package, not the isolated effect of field reduction

July 2022 randomized test recorded 2,000 unique eligible visitors per arm: control 120 successful submissions versus variant 180, or 6.0% versus 9.0%, a 3.0 percentage-point and 50% relative inquiry-conversion increase. CRM-qualified leads were 84 versus 117: qualification among submissions declined from 70% to 65%, while qualified leads per visitor increased from 4.20% to 5.85%, a 39.3% relative increase. Retained the simplified form package and continued monitoring downstream booking/billing; paying-appointment conversion and customer lift were not established by this test. This is distinct from the June/August session-based comparison and is not additional additive lift

Before the July 2022 test, set a 14-day minimum covering weekdays/weekends, approximately 2,000 visitors per variant, a 20% minimum commercially meaningful relative submission-rate improvement and a guardrail that qualified leads per visitor must not deteriorate. Planned a two-sided proportions comparison at the 5% significance level after the planned sample. From supplied counts, the inquiry-rate comparison gives an approximate two-sided p-value of 0.0003 using a pooled normal approximation under independent visitor-level assignment; the screenshot value 0.0004 is an approximation, not an exact reproduced historical output. No sequential monitoring protocol, multiplicity correction or statistically established equivalence in lead qualification is claimed

For July-September 2022 acquisition planning, set a blended $90 paid-media CAC target using an assumed $300 average six-month customer contribution after direct service delivery costs and before acquisition expenditure, with up to 30% allocated to paid acquisition. This was a planning assumption requiring validation by service type, not measured customer lifetime value, audited profit or a universal target for nursing, PCR and consultations. Existing optimized $75 paid-media CAC was 16.7% below that target; this is cost headroom against a target, not profit or realized savings

At $15,000 monthly media spend and $90 target paid-media CAC, forecast approximately 167 new paying customers. A $25 blended CPL target implied 600 leads and approximately 27.8% lead-to-customer conversion. These were planning outputs, not observed results or guaranteed forecasts. Checked customer-service, appointment and healthcare-delivery capacity before spending against the forecast

Reallocated $1,500 of monthly budget from Meta to Google without increasing the $15,000 total: Google $8,250 to $9,750, Meta $6,750 to $5,250. The earlier channel allocation was 55% Google/45% Meta; the revised allocation was 65%/35%. Used service-specific qualification, paying-customer conversion, available Search demand and delivery capacity; reduced weaker Meta segments while retaining commercially valuable audiences/creatives. This allocation decision is not established as the isolated cause of the broader CAC improvement

The earlier acquisition comparison included approximately 550 leads at $15,000 monthly media spend and approximately $27.27 CPL, alongside the already-established approximately 143 new paying customers at approximately $105 paid-media CAC. The optimized comparison remains 675 leads, 200 new paying customers and $75 paid-media CAC, approximately 57 additional customers or 40% growth at unchanged spend. Results reflect combined budget reallocation, campaign refinement, landing-page work and follow-up improvements; do not add this as a second lift or assign the outcome specifically to July-September planning

Used $90 paid-media CAC as a blended planning control: below $90 with stable customer quality, consider increased investment; $90-$105, hold and investigate inefficient segments; above $105 with sufficient conversion volume, reduce or redirect. Prioritized qualification when CPL was low but customer conversion poor, paused scaling when marginal CAC rose, and reduced acquisition pressure for capacity-constrained services. Introduced budget increases gradually, typically 10-15%, then reassessed performance. A strong historical average alone did not justify the next spend increment; the supplied next-$1,000 example explains this rule and is not a separately verified spending incident

Managed marketing follow-up from initial inquiry through booking, post-service communications, repeat bookings and inactive-customer reactivation. Personally built lead/appointment status fields, captured available acquisition source, established segments using service type/booking history/last appointment/consent status, built engagement-based email sequences and content, created customer-service follow-up lists/workflows and produced lifecycle dashboards. Coordinated scheduling friction, unanswered inquiries and availability with operations; CRM and billing records established completed services and repeat customers

Website inquiries entered the WordPress CRM with source, requested service, contact details and lead status for customer-service follow-up. Unbooked inquiries entered a 24-72 hour follow-up queue; confirmed appointments received appropriate pre-service confirmations/reminders. After CRM-confirmed completion, eligible customers received thank-you/feedback follow-up within 24-48 hours; recurring-service follow-up depended on the service, and inactive-customer segments used 30-90 days without recent bookings subject to preferences/suitability. Administrative/marketing workflows supported customer service and operations; clinical recommendations and medical scheduling decisions remained with healthcare staff

Segmented unbooked inquiries for booking assistance, first-time paying customers for service follow-up/second bookings, recurring home-nursing customers for continuity and scheduling support, previous consultation customers for appropriate return-booking convenience, former PCR customers for consent-based general communications where suitable, and inactive customers for reactivation outreach. Supported service delivery, staff availability and customer experience rather than assuming discounts or marketing determined clinical service need

Compared two 90-day periods in 2022: March 1-May 29 baseline and July 1-September 28 optimized. Each included 200 eligible existing customers under the same eligibility definition, though not necessarily the same individuals. Completed repeat paid appointments, excluding each customer original acquisition appointment, increased from 300 to 411: 1.50 to 2.055 per eligible customer, or 150 to 205.5 per 100 customers, a 37% relative frequency increase. Equal eligibility counts and service mix do not establish identical cohorts, randomized assignment or an isolated lifecycle-message effect

The repeat-booking comparison held service-group counts constant in each period: 80 home-nursing customers generated 180 baseline versus 246 optimized repeat appointments; 80 doctor-consultation customers generated 80 versus 110; 40 other eligible-service customers generated 40 versus 55. Totals were 200 eligible customers and 300 versus 411 repeat appointments. This controls the stated service-group proportions; the observed outcome reflects combined messaging, booking convenience, follow-up quality and service delivery, not proof of email automation alone

July-September 2022 reactivation combined consent-based email and customer-service follow-up with messages based on past services. Of 500 eligible inactive customers, 400 were successfully contacted, 100 replied or made an inquiry and 40 completed another paid appointment: 8.0% reactivation against the eligible base or 10.0% against contacted customers. Reactivated customers were existing customers, excluded from new-customer acquisition counts. Eligible repeat appointments could overlap repeat-booking reporting under its rules; exact overlap is not established, so do not add these outcomes as independent incremental customers or appointments

Used CRM/billing records to distinguish first-to-second paid booking rate, repeat paid appointments per eligible existing customer, reactivation after inactivity, bookings following outreach, activity-based retention and revenue from previously paying customers. Reviewed sequences generating clicks without completed appointments and used customer-service/operations feedback to improve messaging, scheduling communications and booking convenience. The quantified frequency and reactivation results do not establish numerical retention percentage, second-booking rate, repeat revenue, lifetime value or causal outreach incrementality; no randomized lifecycle holdout was established

Personally configured a Google Data Studio/Looker Studio acquisition and customer-economics dashboard, defined its KPIs, connected sources and maintained reporting logic. Combined native Google Ads and Analytics connectors for Google Ads/GA4/Universal Analytics reporting with Meta scheduled CSV exports and WordPress CRM booking/status/payment CSV exports. Used Google Sheets formulas and lookup tables for file-based consolidation and reconciliation; source access combined connectors and exports rather than assuming every source passed through the same integration

Refreshed PrimaCare reporting daily after Meta and CRM exports were updated, reviewed campaign pacing/acquisition daily, conducted weekly stakeholder performance reviews and prepared monthly management summaries. Business ownership reviewed acquisition spend, CAC, appointments and revenue; sales/customer service reviewed lead quality, follow-up and booking bottlenecks; marketing reviewed pacing, CPL, qualification and channel efficiency. The dashboard was daily refreshed, not a real-time customer-revenue warehouse

Defined CPL as advertising spend per unique recorded lead, qualification rate as CRM-qualified leads per recorded lead, lead-to-customer rate as first-time paying customers per lead, and paid-media CAC as spend per attributed new paying customer. Reported repeat-booking frequency as completed repeat appointments per eligible existing customer and pacing as month-to-date actual versus planned spend. Kept platform interactions distinct from CRM-confirmed commercial outcomes and reused the established optimized monthly scorecard rather than creating a second performance result

Reconciled records using contact identifiers, available campaign/source information, booking IDs and payment status; investigated duplicate/invalid inquiries, customers who did not progress to paid appointments, attribution-window differences, reporting delays and missing source information. CRM and billing records established actual appointments and paying customers, with each acquired customer assigned to one channel for deduplicated acquisition reporting. This did not require advertising conversions to equal CRM customers

Used the dashboard to identify cheaper Meta inquiries with weaker downstream booking performance alongside higher-intent Google Search inquiries, informing the already-established monthly Meta-to-Google budget reallocation while holding total spend constant. Considered customer economics and qualification rather than clicks/CPL alone. The existing CAC/customer improvement reflects combined campaign, landing-page, qualification and follow-up changes; it is not a separate lift attributable solely to the dashboard

Standardized reporting exports, maintained reusable reconciliation formulas and presented consistent KPIs in a shared dashboard instead of rebuilding separate spreadsheets each reporting cycle. The workflow included file-based imports and review rather than a fully automated custom API integration or real-time warehouse; the user subsequently confirmed the supplied reporting-preparation timings as actual historical figures

Reduced daily advertising/CRM consolidation from 60 to 15 minutes, weekly management-report preparation from 3 hours to 45 minutes, and monthly reporting preparation from 8 to 2 hours: a 75% reduction for each recurring activity. Achieved through standardized exports, reusable reconciliation formulas and shared Data Studio/Looker Studio reporting. These are user-confirmed historical timings, correcting the earlier proposed label; overlap between daily, weekly and monthly activities is not established, so do not sum them into cumulative or annual hours saved. This is separate from appointment-scheduling time reduction

roles.title: Digital Marketing & Performance Manager
roles.context: Agency serving 25-30 clients, with 20-25 concurrent paid accounts

clients.name: Al Aaraf Jewelers
clients.industry: Luxury jewelry retail: physical showroom plus a newly launched direct-to-consumer e-commerce store
clients.ownership: Sole owner of the client's entire marketing function

clients.name: J5 Hotels
clients.industry: Hospitality: a 3-star hotel working toward 4-star, a 4-star hotel and villa rentals

clients.name: Bagason Industries
clients.industry: FMCG: condiments, canned foods, juices and milks, cooking oils

clients.name: Qahwaty
clients.industry: Specialty coffee cafe, 2 branches (DIFC and Sharjah)

clients.name: Late Lounge
clients.industry: Cafe: brunch, desserts, all-day Emirati breakfast and specialty coffee

clients.name: Forever Rose (Jumeirah shop and cafe)
clients.industry: Luxury preserved roses, perfumes and gifts shop, with an adjacent cafe run as a separate business

facts.text: Managed approximately USD $272K in combined monthly client advertising spend, with peak months around $320K, across 20-25 concurrent paid accounts within a 25-30-client portfolio by 2022 (retained clients plus project-level campaigns for large brands). This is aggregate monthly portfolio spend, not lifetime cumulative spend, a single account budget or agency self-promotion expenditure; execution was shared with the team under the candidate's portfolio/performance ownership

Approximate monthly portfolio allocation: Google $136,000 (50%), Meta $108,800 (40%) and LinkedIn $27,200 (10%), totaling $272K; a core-channel approximation in which the less commonly used Snapchat, TikTok, Twitter and Reddit spend is not broken out; not a per-account allocation or a verified total across all employment months

Managed Google Search, Display, YouTube, remarketing and Shopping where relevant; Meta conversion, lead-generation, traffic and retargeting campaigns; LinkedIn sponsored content/B2B lead generation; and Snapchat, TikTok, Twitter and Reddit on specific client accounts. Responsibilities covered setup, keyword research, bidding, segmentation, creative testing, negative keywords, conversion tracking, pacing and client reporting, with execution distributed across the team
